problem:
$$
{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}=3 \\ -2{x}_{1}-4{x}_{2}=6 \\ {x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=-3\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the system of linear equations shown above. If the general least-squares solution of the system is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}a \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}b \\ c\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R
$$

what is the value of $a-\frac{3b}{c}?$

activity_context.topic_title: The Least-Squares Solution of a Linear System (With Collinearity)

feedback.problem:
$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=1 \\ 5{x}_{1}-5{x}_{2}=0 \\ 2{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the system of linear equations shown above. If the general least-squares solution of the system is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}a \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}b \\ c\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R
$$

what is the value of $30a+\frac{b}{c}?$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we write our system in matrix form as $Ax=b,$ where 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 5 & -5 \\ 2 & -2\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$

The least-squares solution of $Ax=b$ satisfies the corresponding normal equation:

$$
{A}^{T}\,Ax={A}^{T}b
$$

Notice that the columns of $A$ are linearly dependent. So first, let's write down the normal equation in matrix form:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 & 2 \\ -1 & -5 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 5 & -5 \\ 2 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 & 2 \\ -1 & -5 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}30 & -30 \\ -30 & 30\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the system corresponding to the final matrix equation using Gaussian elimination, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}30 & -30 & 1 \\ -30 & 30 & -1\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}30 & -30 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we have 

$$
{x}_{1}=\frac{1}{30}+{x}_{2}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{30}+{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{30} \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
30a+\frac{b}{c}=30\cdot \frac{1}{30}+\frac{1}{1}=2.
$$
